brief_extract: There are few things more annoying than to hear people say that it is a pity China was ever awakened by the West. I shall never forget the reply made to me one afternoon by Madame Quo Tai-Chi, wife of the Chinese Ambassador, when speaking of the terrible suffering of the war out there, of the bombs and destruction, I exclaimed to her : " I should think you sometimes wish we foreigners had never come to China." She looked at me in surprise and said : " Oh, but we would not go back to the past, in spite of this war. We couldn't do without the thought that the West has brought us besides so many good things—trains, electric light, telephones and wireless." For good or ill the Chinese would not wish to be left behind in a backwater while the great seekers into the secrets of science pour forth in other countries its multiple riches.

GLADYS SCOTT visits a Government Training Centre

SO wrote Pliny in the very long ago, and in case, like me, your knowledge of Latin does not encompass more than amo, amas, amat, and, unlike me, you have no voluminous Dictionary of Quotations to lend you erudition, I will translate: “Our studies are advanced by cheerfulness.”

Now, this state of affairs is so true of a Government Training Centre I was privileged to visit in a London Suburb recently that I offer the quotation gratis as a motto for the establishment. Everyone, except the very newly-born, must know something of the activities of these Training Centres, and it is not of them that I primarily wish to write, for such technical details can be obtained from pamphlets, Labour Exchanges, Citizens’ Advice Bureaux, and were the subject of a brief review in the April issue of this magazine.

SO wrote Pliny in the very long ago, and in case, like me, your knowledge of Latin does not encompass more than amo, amas, amat, and, unlike me, you have no voluminous Dictionary of Quotations to lend you erudition, I will translate: “Our studies are advanced by cheerfulness.”
